overview.about: The FIFA World Cup is the world's most-watched sporting event — football's championship of nations, contested every four years since Uruguay hosted and won the first tournament in 1930. Only eight countries have ever lifted the trophy, and Brazil lead the way with five. The 2030 edition breaks the mould: to mark the competition's centenary it is co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal across Africa and Europe, while three opening matches return to South America — Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay — where the very first final was played in 1930. Forty-eight teams contest 104 matches over roughly six weeks, and Spain arrive as holders after winning the 2026 final.
overview.nextEvent: The centenary World Cup runs 8 June – 21 July 2030 and is the first ever spread across three continents and three confederations. The main tournament — 101 of the 104 matches — is staged in Morocco, Spain and Portugal, with three symbolic opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to honour the 1930 original. Spain defend the title they won in 2026.

airportTransfer: The 2030 tournament has 101 matches in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, plus centenary matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay. Select the match city before arranging airport transport.
arrivalWindow: Book after FIFA confirms your fixture city
flightTip: Avoid non-refundable multi-city flights until the published fixture list confirms where your match will be played.
stayGuidance: Do not use one base for the whole tournament: the 101-match programme spans Morocco, Portugal and Spain, while the centenary matches are in South America.
bookingAdvice: Compare accommodation once you know the match city and kickoff date; the official schedule determines the practical airport and hotel base.
transportTip: Plan from the match city, not the host country
transportDetail: The six-country format makes a single transport plan unreliable. Check FIFA's confirmed fixture and stadium details before buying intercity travel.
eventDayTip: Keep the official match details with you
eventDayDetail: FIFA says the South American centenary matches are played before the opening matches in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, so travel timing depends on the fixture you attend.
